# MVP Site HTTP API

## Overview

MVP-site example app: aggregates the site (miners, a powermeter, a mining pool) via the MDK protocol client.

Every path is relative to `/`, where the Gateway serves these routes. The OpenAPI 3.1 document is [`openapi.json`](openapi.json).

Purpose is the operation's declared description. Access is the `spec.rbac` requirement the Gateway checks, a verb on a resource; it does not
mean any particular caller is allowed. "Not declared" marks something the declaration does not state.

## Operations

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Request | Responses |
| ------ | ---- | ------- | ------ | ------- | --------- |
| `GET` | `/site/overview` | Live site snapshot assembled from `telemetry.pull` across all workers: all miners, site power consumption from powermeters, and pool data from all minerpool workers. Workers that are down are listed in `unavailableWorkers` with their device counts, since their devices cannot be read. | `get` on `site/site/overview` | Bearer token | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |
| `GET` | `/site/history` | Historical telemetry from the workers' persisted tail-logs (`telemetry.pull` type `logs`). `metric=hashrate` reads pool stats-history (H/s, the unit the pool contracts declare; all pools summed by default; pass `deviceId` for one pool). `metric=site-hashrate` reads the miners' own snap tail-logs summed across all miners (MH/s; pass `deviceId` for one miner). `metric=power` reads site powermeter series (all meters summed by default; pass `deviceId` for one meter). `metric=temperature` reads sensor tail-logs, averaged by default; this example ships no sensor Worker, so it returns empty unless one is added. Defaults to the last hour. | `get` on `site/site/history` | Bearer token, `metric` (query), `deviceId` (query), `start` (query), `end` (query) | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |
| `GET` | `/site/access` | The signed-in user's identity, the roles `spec.rbac` binds to them, which site routes they may call, and which miners they may send each command to. Advisory, for the UI: the Gateway and the Kernel enforce the same policy on every call. | `get` on `site/site/access` | Bearer token | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |
| `GET` | `/site/activity` | Every miner command attempted on this site, newest first, refused ones included: who sent it (the operator, via the site app), the roles they held, the command, the target device, and the outcome. Reads the Kernel's write-command log (`command.log`), so the caller needs `commands: read`. | `get` on `site/site/activity` | Bearer token, `limit` (query) | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |
| `POST` | `/site/miners/{deviceId}/command` | Dispatches the `setPowerMode` capability command to a single miner through Kernel. The new mode appears on the next telemetry poll. | `create` on `site/site/miners/:deviceId/command` | Bearer token, `deviceId` (path), JSON body (required) | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `422`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |
| `POST` | `/site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | Dispatches the `setupPools` capability command to a single miner through Kernel. Pools from the request body take precedence; with no body the site-wide default from `config/site.deploy.json` (`worker.pools`) is applied. The miner reboots to pick up the new pools, so expect it to drop offline briefly. | `create` on `site/site/miners/:deviceId/pools` | Bearer token, `deviceId` (path), JSON body | `200`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `422`, `429`, `502`, `503`, `504` |

## Errors

An error response's body is `{ statusCode, error, message }`:

- `statusCode`: The HTTP status, repeated
- `error`: The HTTP status text, such as `Unauthorized`
- `message`: The `ERR_*` code, followed by a colon, a space, and a detail when there is one. For a body the Gateway cannot read, or a
  request that fails the route's schema, Fastify's message. Otherwise, the HTTP status text.

### Errors on every app route

What the Gateway and the app runtime answer on every app route, in the order a request meets each stage on a Gateway with an RBAC authority.
Each code is listed once, not with each operation that can answer it. A Rule row covers codes no single page can list.

| Stage | Code | Status | Fires when | Fix |
| ----- | ---- | ------ | ---------- | --- |
| Host check | `ERR_GATEWAY_HOST_NOT_ALLOWED` | `403` | The request's `Host` header is missing, or names a host the Gateway does not serve. The Gateway serves loopback on its port, its own bind address, and each `allowedHosts` entry. With `trustProxy` set, `X-Forwarded-Host` is checked instead. | Call the Gateway by a host it serves, or have the operator add the host to `allowedHosts` |
| Rate limit | `ERR_RATE_LIMITED` | `429` | The caller's address has sent more requests than the Gateway's `rateLimit` allows in its time window, `300` a minute by default | Wait for the time window to pass, then retry |
| Authentication | `ERR_AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED` | `401` | The request carries no bearer token, or one that fails verification, such as an expired or revoked token | Sign in, and send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| Custom verifier | Rule | `4XX` | On a Gateway with no RBAC authority, an `auth: true` route runs the operator's `authVerifier` after the rate limit and before the body is read, in place of authentication and authorization. The route answers the verifier's own `4xx` error when it throws one whose message starts with `ERR_`. Otherwise it answers `401` `ERR_AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED`: when none is configured, when the verifier refuses the caller, and when it throws anything else. The operator who supplies the verifier documents its codes, and the `@tetherto/mdk-gateway` README describes the hook. | Send the credentials the operator's verifier expects |
| Body parsing | Rule | `415` | A request other than `GET` carries a body in a content type the Gateway has no parser for; it parses `application/json` and `text/plain`. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's `Unsupported Media Type`, not an `ERR_*` code. | Send the body in the content type the operation declares |
| Body parsing | Rule | `413` | A request other than `GET` carries a body larger than the Gateway's `bodyLimit`, `1048576` bytes by default. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's `Request body is too large`, not an `ERR_*` code. | Send a smaller body, or have the operator raise `bodyLimit` |
| Body parsing | Rule | `400` | A request other than `GET` carries a body that does not parse as its content type, such as malformed JSON, or an empty body sent as `application/json`. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's parse error, not an `ERR_*` code. | Send a body that parses as its `Content-Type` |
| Authorization | `ERR_AUTH_FORBIDDEN` | `403` | No `spec.rbac` rule grants the caller the route's verb on its resource, or the Gateway's copy of the policy is stale. The message names the caller, the verb, and the resource, and the Gateway's decision log names the reason. | Ask an operator for a role that grants the call in `spec.rbac` |
| Body validation | Rule | `400` | The request's path parameters, query, or body fail the schema the app's route table declares for the route. The message is Fastify's validation error, not an `ERR_*` code. | Send the parameters and body the operation declares |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_BAD_REQUEST` | `400` | The app runtime refused the request envelope the Gateway sent: malformed, with no `routeId`, or with an `actor` that is not an access token | Run the Gateway and the app runtime from the same MDK release |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_ROUTE_IS_STREAM` | `400` | The Gateway called a stream route as a unary one, such as when the Gateway and the app runtime loaded different route tables | Restart the Gateway and the app runtime on the same route table |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_ROUTE_NOT_STREAM` | `400` | The Gateway called a unary route as a stream, such as when the Gateway and the app runtime loaded different route tables | Restart the Gateway and the app runtime on the same route table |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | `404` | The app runtime has no route with the id the Gateway forwarded, such as when the Gateway and the app runtime loaded different route tables | Restart the Gateway and the app runtime on the same route table |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `502` | The app runtime answered in a different protocol version from the Gateway's client | Run the Gateway and the app runtime from the same MDK release |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | `502` | The app runtime is unreachable, does not allow the Gateway's key, or closed or garbled its reply | Check that the app runtime is running and allows the Gateway's key, then retry. A call that changes something may have run before its reply was lost, so check its result first. |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | `503` | The app runtime has not published its key file: it has not started yet, or it has stopped | Start the app runtime, or retry once it has started |
| Forwarding | `ERR_APP_RUNTIME_TIMEOUT` | `504` | The app runtime sent no answer, or no stream head, within the Gateway's `appTimeoutMs`, `60000` by default. The Gateway stops waiting, but the route's controller is not stopped, so the call may still complete. | Retry a call that only reads. For a call that changes something, check its result or the device's state before sending it again. If it repeats, check the route's controller, or raise `appTimeoutMs`. |
| Controller | Rule | Varies | An error the route's controller throws arrives with its `statusCode` when that is `400` or more, else `403` for `ERR_KERNEL_ACTION_FORBIDDEN` (the Kernel refused the call under `spec.rbac`), `400` for any other `ERR_*` error, and `500` for anything else. A message that does not start with `ERR_` arrives as the status text, such as `Internal Server Error`, and the app runtime logs the original. The app's route table declares the codes its controllers throw. | Act on the code as the operation declares it |
| Controller | Rule | Varies | A controller that passes on an error from its Kernel client relays the client's `ERR_*` code, which arrives as `400` by the controller rule, or `403` for `ERR_KERNEL_ACTION_FORBIDDEN`. The `@tetherto/mdk-client` README documents the client's transport codes, and the `@tetherto/mdk-kernel` README the Kernel's refusals. | Act on the code as the package that throws it documents |

### Errors the operations declare

The application error codes the operations declare, the HTTP status each arrives with, when it fires and what the caller does about it. "Not
declared" marks what the declaration does not state.

| Code | Status | Operations | Fires when | Fix |
| ---- | ------ | ---------- | ---------- | --- |
| `ERR_COMMAND_REJECTED` | `422` | `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The Kernel refused the command without a code. A fallback: the current Kernel always sends one. | Retry; if it repeats, check the Kernel log for the refusal |
| `ERR_DEVICE_ID_REQUIRED` | `400` | `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The `deviceId` path segment is empty | Put the miner's `deviceId` in the path |
| `ERR_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` | `404` | `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The Kernel refused the command: no such device | Send a `deviceId` from `GET /site/overview` |
| `ERR_INVALID_DATE_RANGE` | `400` | `GET /site/history` | `start` is not before `end` | Send a `start` earlier than `end` |
| `ERR_INVALID_POOLS` | `400` | `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | `pools` is an empty list, or an entry has an empty `url` or `worker_name` | Send one to three pools, each with a non-empty `url` and `worker_name` |
| `ERR_KERNEL_ACTION_FORBIDDEN` | `403` | `GET /site/overview`, `GET /site/history`, `GET /site/access`, `GET /site/activity`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The Kernel refused the call for the caller's roles, or for this app's service account | Grant the caller, or this app's service account, the access the route needs in `spec.rbac` |
| `ERR_MDK_CLIENT_UNAVAILABLE` | `400` | `GET /site/overview`, `GET /site/history`, `GET /site/access`, `GET /site/activity`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The Kernel client could not reach the Kernel (no `kernelKey`, a failed connection or a closed channel) | Check the Kernel is running and reachable from the app runtime, then retry |
| `ERR_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` | `401` | `GET /site/access`, `GET /site/activity` | The request carries no signed-in identity | Sign in, and send the access token |
| `ERR_UNKNOWN_DEVICE_ID` | `400` | `GET /site/history` | `deviceId` matches none of the requested metric's devices (mining pools, for `hashrate`). A metric with no devices at all answers an empty log instead. | Send a `deviceId` from `GET /site/overview`, or omit it for every device |
| `ERR_WORKER_NOT_ROUTABLE` | `422` | `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/command`, `POST /site/miners/{deviceId}/pools` | The Kernel refused the command: the device's Worker is not ready or not healthy. Any other refusal code the Kernel returns for the command also arrives as 422. | Retry once the Worker reports ready and healthy in `GET /site/overview` |
